rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse answers an earlier assurance: God cared for Muhammad when weak and orphaned, raised him greatly, and therefore will not abandon him now.
rows.anchor: كانت طاعاتك في ذلك الوقت أكرم أم الساعة ؟ فلا بد من أن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here wajada means to know, with Muhammad and an orphan as the two objects: God knew him orphaned and sheltered him.
rows.anchor: المنصوبان مفعولا وجد والوجود من الله ، والمعنى ألم يعلمك الله يتيما

rows.speaker: أهل الأخبار
rows.claim: They report that Muhammad's father died before his birth, his mother when he was six, and his grandfather two years later when he was eight.
rows.anchor: عبد الله بن عبد المطلب فيما ذكره أهل الأخبار توفي وأم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حامل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Talib then raised and supported Muhammad until his mission; the author says he never again appeared an orphan.
rows.anchor: فكان أبو طالب هو الذي يكفل رسول الله بعد جده إلى أن بعثه الله للنبوة

rows.speaker: أبو طالب
rows.claim: In a report to al-Abbas, Abu Talib said he kept Muhammad beside him constantly, guarded him, and even placed him in his own bed.
rows.anchor: إني ضممته إلي فكيف لا أفارقه ساعة من ليل ولا نهار ؛ ولا أأتمن عليه أحدا

rows.speaker: أبو طالب
rows.claim: Abu Talib recounted Muhammad's modesty, fragrant presence, and miraculous appearances in bed, and said he never lied or joined ignorant children's play.
rows.anchor: فرأيت الكراهة في وجهه لكنه كره أن يخالفني ، وقال : يا عماه اصرف بوجهك عني

rows.speaker: أبو طالب
rows.claim: Abu Talib recalled that Muhammad began meals invoking the One God and ended them praising God, unlike the family's usual practice.
rows.anchor: وكان يقول في أول الطعام : بسم الله الأحد . فإذا فرغ من طعامه قال : الحمدلله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes yatim as a unique pearl: Muhammad was peerless among Quraysh, and God gave him Abu Talib as refuge.
rows.anchor: التفسير الثاني لليتيم : أنه من قولهم درة يتيمة ، والمعنى ألم يجدك واحدا في قريش عديم النظير فآواك ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading fa-awā can mean either that God sheltered him or showed him mercy.
rows.anchor: وقرىء فأوى وهو على معنيين : إما من أواه بمعنى آواه ، وإما من أوى له إذا رحمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine reminders of favors strengthen the Prophet and promise their continuation; Pharaoh's reminder was self-serving, asking why Moses would not serve him.
rows.anchor: أن ذلك يحسن إذا قصد بذلك أن يقوي قلبه ويعده بدوام النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promise to complete His favor resembles a sound pregnancy brought to term: abandoning the work of nurturing would be blameworthy.
rows.anchor: وامتنان الله بزيادة نعمه ، كأنه يقول : مالك تقطع عني رجاءك ألست شرعت في تربيتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He contrasts a former community whose fourth was a dog with Muhammad's community, whose private conversations have God as the fourth.
rows.anchor: نظيره ما قاله بعضهم : { ثلاثة رابعهم كلبهم } ( الكهف : 22 ) في تلك الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repaying benefaction is a lifelong, weightier debt than a financial loan; since God's gifts cannot be repaid, the servant should extend the same care to orphans and needy seekers and remember God's favor.
rows.anchor: فكأن العبد يقول : إلهي أخرجتني من العدم إلى الوجود بشرا سويا ، طاهر الظاهر نجس الباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The practical answer to unrepayable divine gifts is to shelter orphans, guide and aid God's servants, and continually remember that even this service depends on God's help.
rows.anchor: فيقول تعالى الطريق إلى ذلك أن تفعل في حق عبيدي ما فعلته في حقك ، كنت يتيما فآويتك

none: bare verse heading and transition only

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says Muhammad was among a misguided people and God guided him to monotheism; al-Suddi says he followed his people's religion for forty years; Mujahid says he lacked guidance to his religion.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي : { ووجدك ضالا } يعني كافرا في قوم ضلال فهداك للتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those alleging prior unbelief cite 42:52, 12:3, and 39:65 as support for ignorance of revelation and the conditional warning against association.
rows.anchor: ما كنت تدرى ما الكتاب ولا الإيمان } ( الشورى : 52 ) وقوله : { وإن كنت من قبله لمن الغافلين

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority of scholars agree that the Prophet never disbelieved in God, even for an instant.
rows.anchor: وأما الجمهور من العلماء فقد اتفقوا على أنه عليه السلام ما كفر بالله لحظة واحدة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu'tazila deem even a possible period of unbelief rationally impermissible because it would repel people from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ثم قالت المعتزلة : هذا غير جائز عقلا لما فيه من التنفير

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The author's theological school allows that possibility in reason, but says scriptural evidence shows it did not occur, citing the declaration that the Prophet neither strayed nor erred.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الدليل السمعي قام على أن هذا الجائز لم يقع وهو قوله تعالى : { ما ضل صاحبكم وما غوى }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك وشهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: They interpret the phrase as ignorance of divine favor and the religious law, which God then taught through revelation.
rows.anchor: أحدها : ما روي عن ابن عباس والحسن والضحاك وشهر بن حوشب : { ووجدك ضالا } عن معالم النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says Halima lost the child while returning him to his grandfather; at Hubal the idols fell and a voice foretold their destruction by him.
rows.anchor: ضل عن مرضعته حليمة حين أرادت أن ترده إلى جده حتى دخلت إلى هبل وشكت ذلك إليه فتساقطت الأصنام

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits a report attributed to the Prophet that, as a lost and hungry boy separated from his grandfather, God guided him back.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : ما روي مرفوعا أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : ( ضللت عن جدي عبد المطلب وأنا صبي ضائع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says God returned Muhammad to his grandfather through an enemy, just as He preserved Moses through an enemy.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : رده الله إلى جده بيد عدوه كما فعل بموسى حين حفظه على يد عدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says a disbeliever leading his camel lost Muhammad on a journey with Khadija's servant Maysara; Gabriel appeared as a man and guided him to the caravan.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : أنه عليه السلام لما خرج مع غلام خديجة ميسرة أخذ كافر بزمام بعيره حتى ضل ،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also said that Abu Talib took Muhammad to Syria, where he lost the route and God guided him.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن أبا طالب خرج به إلى الشأم فضل عن الطريق فهداه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using the idiom of water submerged in milk, the verse can mean Muhammad was overwhelmed among Meccan unbelievers until God strengthened him to manifest the faith.
rows.anchor: وخامسها : يقال : ضل الماء في اللبل إذا صار مغمورا ، فمعنى الآية كنت مغمورا بين الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A solitary tree in the wilderness is called ḍāllah: Muhammad was the lone tree bearing faith and knowledge in a barren land, and through him God guided people; this resembles the saying that wisdom is the believer's lost property.
rows.anchor: وسادسها : العرب تسمي الشجرة الفريدة في الفلاة ضالة ، كأنه تعالى يقول : كانت تلك البلاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that as a child he was without knowledge of God, like all people at birth; ḍāll here means devoid of knowledge, not holding a false belief.
rows.anchor: فخلق فيك العقل والهداية والمعرفة / والمراد من الضال الخالي عن العلم لا الموصوف بالاعتقاد الخطأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may have been unaware of his future prophethood, which neither he expected nor the Jews and Christians thought could belong outside Israel.
rows.anchor: وثامنها : كنت ضالا عن النبوة ما كنت تطمع في ذلك ولا خطر شيء من ذلك في قلبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A singular address may refer to Muhammad's people: they were astray, and God guided them through him and his law.
rows.anchor: وتاسعها : أنه قد يخاطب السيد ، ويكون المراد قومه فقوله : { ووجدك ضالا } أي وجد قومك ضلالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean he stood apart from the misguided; God guided him to mix with them and call them to the manifest religion.
rows.anchor: وعاشرها : وجدك ضالا عن الضالين منفردا عنهم مجانبا لدينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation concerns his wish to leave Quraysh but inability to depart without permission; God guided the emigration, the route to Umm Ma'bad, and the events with Suraqa.
rows.anchor: الحادي عشر : وجدك ضالا عن الهجرة ، متحيرا في يد قريش متمنيا فراقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He desired the Kaaba as qibla but did not know if it would be granted, then God directed him to the desired prayer direction.
rows.anchor: الثاني عشر : ضالا عن القبلة ، فإنه كان يتمنى أن تجعل الكعبة قبلة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Gabriel's first appearance, Muhammad did not know who he was and was frightened; God guided him until he recognized Gabriel.
rows.anchor: الثالث عشر : أنه حين ظهرها له جبريل عليه السلام في أول أمره ما كان يعرف أهو جبريل أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍalāl can mean love, as in Jacob's deep love for Joseph; God guided Muhammad to laws by which he could serve his beloved Lord.
rows.anchor: الرابع عشر : الضلال بمعنى المحبة كما في قوله : { إنك لفى ضلالك القديم } ( يوسف : 95 ) أي محبتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He lacked worldly and commercial know-how, then God guided him to profitable trade that drew Khadija's interest; his attention had been devoted to religion.
rows.anchor: الخامس عشر : ضالا عن أمور الدنيا لا تعرف التجارة ونحوها ، ثم هديتك حتى ربحت تجارتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can mean that he was lost and powerless among people who mistreated and rejected him, until God made him their commander.
rows.anchor: السادس عشر : { ووجدك ضالا } أي ضائعا في قومك ؛ كانوا يؤذونك ، ولا يرضون بك رعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may refer to not knowing the route through the heavens until God guided him on the night journey and ascension.
rows.anchor: السابع عشر : كنت ضالا ما كنت تهتدي على طريق السموات فهديتك إذ عرجت بك إلى السموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By analogy with a woman being led into error, ḍalāl can mean forgetting: in awe on the night journey he forgot words of praise until taught to say he could not enumerate God's praise.
rows.anchor: الثامن عشر : ووجدك ضالا أي ناسيا لقوله تعالى : { أن تضل إحداهما } ( البقرة : 282 )

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali transmits the Prophet's account that God twice prevented him from joining pre-Islamic nighttime entertainment; he fell asleep until sunlight, and afterward never intended evil until his mission.
rows.anchor: العشرون : روى علي عليه السلام عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( ما هممت بشيء مما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation gives the Prophet's story of twice being prevented by sleep from joining young men at a wedding celebration, after which he never intended evil.
rows.anchor: فما أيقظني إلا مس الشمس ، قال فجئت صاحبي ، فقال ما فعلت ؟

none: bare verse heading and transition only

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀʾil derives from having dependents; the word also denotes poverty even without dependents, and is related to the terms in 4:3 and 9:28.
rows.anchor: العائل هو ذو العيلة ، وذكرنا ذلك عند قوله : { أن لا * تعولوا } ( النساء : 3 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The famous interpretation is that Muhammad was poor; Abdullah's codex reads 'destitute,' with a variant ʿaylan.
rows.anchor: الأول : وهو المشهور أن المراد هو الفقير ، ويدل عليه ما روى أنه في مصحف عبد الله : / ( ووجدك عديما )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account traces enrichment through Abu Talib's care, Khadija's wealth, Abu Bakr's money, the Ansar, and later spoils already known to be coming.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى أغناه بتربية أبي طالب ، ولما اختلت أحوال أبي طالب أغناه ( الله ) بمال خديجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Muhammad worried that famine relief would exhaust Khadija's money; she summoned Quraysh and offered him a great sum to spend or keep as he wished.
rows.anchor: روي أنه عليه السلام : ( دخل على خديجة وهو مغموم ، فقالت له مالك ، فقال : الزمان زمان قحط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view is that God enriched him with companions: Umar objected to Muslims worshipping secretly, and God promised support through believers, Abu Bakr's wealth, and Umar's influence.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أغناه بأصحابه كانوا يعبدون الله سرا حتى قال عمر حين أسلم : أبرز أتعبد اللات جهرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Enrichment may mean contentment: Muhammad became indifferent between gold and stone, needing only God; true richness is independence from things, and he chose poverty when offered wealth.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أغناك بالقناعة فصرت بحال يستوي عندك الحجر والذهب ، لا تجد في قلبك سوى ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that God supplied the proofs and arguments he lacked by revealing the Qur'an and teaching him.
rows.anchor: الرابع : كنت عائلا عن البراهين والحجج ، فأنزل الله عليك القرآن ، وعلمك مالم تكن تعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another meaning is that he had many dependents, namely his community, and God sufficed him; alternatively, God enriched his ignorant, poor people with his knowledge and guidance.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني في تفسير العائل : أنت كنت كثير العيال وهم الأمة ، فكفاك . وقيل فأغناهم بك لأنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made him an orphan so he would understand orphans' needs and defend their rights; Joseph avoided eating his fill lest he forget the hungry.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن يعرف قدر اليتامى فيقوم بحقهم وصلاح أمرهم ، ومن ذلك كان يوسف عليه السلام لا يشبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed wisdom is the shared designation of orphanhood, which would occasion special honor; a report also urges honoring a child named Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : ليكون اليتيم مشاركا له في الاسم فيكرم لأجل ذلك ، ومن ذلك قال عليه السلام : ( إذا سميتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without parents to rely on, he depended on God from earliest childhood, like Abraham entrusting himself to God and Mary's answer that provision came from Him.
rows.anchor: فسلب عنه الولدان حتى لا يعتمد من أول صباه إلى آخر عمره على أحد سوى الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orphan's faults are publicly visible; God chose this condition so observers would find no flaw in Muhammad and no objection to his prophethood.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : أن العادة جارية بأن اليتيم لا تخفى عيوبه بل تظهر ، وربما زادوا على الموجود فاختار تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His orphanhood makes clear that his excellence came from God, since a father normally works to educate and discipline a child.
rows.anchor: وخامسها : جعله يتيما ليعلم كل أحد أن فضيلته من الله ابتداء لأن الذي له أب ، فإن أباه يسعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orphanhood and poverty are usually deficiencies, so Muhammad's becoming the most honored despite both overturns custom and functions as a miracle.
rows.anchor: وسادسها : أن اليتم والفقر نقص في حق / الخلق ، فلما صار محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام / مع هذين الوصفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning these circumstances keeps the Prophet mindful of them and prevents self-admiration.
rows.anchor: الحكمة أن لا ينسى نفسه فيقع في العجب

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The judge criticizes a report in which the Prophet asks why others received special favors: prophets only ask with permission, and God's reply sounds reproachful.
rows.anchor: فهل يصح هذا الحديث قلنا : طعن القاضي في هذا الخبر فقال : إن الأنبياء عليهم السلام لا يسألون مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variant fa-la takhar means do not scowl at the orphan; treat the orphan as God treated you, echoing the command to do good as God did.
rows.anchor: وقرىء فلا تكهر ، أي لا تعبس وجهك إليه ، والمعنى عامله بمثل ما عاملتك به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic saying warns believers to fear God regarding someone who has no protector but Him.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله عليه السلام : ( الله الله فيمن ليس له إلا الله )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says it was reported that the verse came down when the Prophet cried out over Khadija's child.
rows.anchor: وروي : أنها نزلت حين صاح النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على ولد خديجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report has God tell Moses he became a leader of creation because he compassionately carried back an exhausted lamb; kindness to an orphan is still more deserving.
rows.anchor: قال : أتذكر حين هربت منك السخلة ، فلما قدرت عليها قلت : أتعبت نفسك ثم حملتها

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas transmits a saying that an orphan's tears fall into the Merciful's hand, and God promises Paradise to the person who comforts the child.
rows.anchor: عن أنس عن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( إذا بكى اليتيم وقعت دموعه في كف الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahr means confronting someone with rebuking, repellent speech.
rows.anchor: يقال : نهره وانتهره إذا استقبله بكلام يزجره

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan's preferred meaning is a seeker of religious knowledge; the sequence moves from God's favors to care for orphans, then learners, then gratitude.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : وهو اختيار الحسن أن المراد منه من يسأل العلم ونظيره من وجه : { عبس وتولى * أن جاءه الاعمى } ( عبس : 1 ، 2 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the command covers any supplicant; the author cites three episodes in which the Qur'an reproached the Prophet over treatment of poor people.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن المراد مطلق السائل ولقد عائب الله رسوله في القرآن في شأن الفقراء في ثلاثة مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the first episode, blind Ibn Umm Maktum interrupted Quraysh leaders to ask for instruction, and the Prophet frowned; the author links it to the opening of al-Abasa.
rows.anchor: أنه كان جالسا وحوله صناديد قريش ، إذ جاء ابن أم مكتوم الضرير ، فتخطى رقاب الناس حتى جلس بين يديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the second, the Prophet considered Quraysh's request for separate gatherings for elites and poor until the command to remain with those who pray came.
rows.anchor: والثالث : كان جالسا فجاءه عثمان بعذق من ثمر فوضعه بين يديه فأراد أن يأكل فوقف سائل بالباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the third, a beggar sought dates set before the Prophet by Uthman; Uthman objected to giving them, then bought them back from the beggar three times, and the Prophet asked if he was a seller or asker.
rows.anchor: كان جالسا فجاءه عثمان بعذق من ثمر فوضعه بين يديه فأراد أن يأكل فوقف سائل بالباب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the greatest blessing as the Qur'an; telling it means reciting, teaching others to recite, and explaining its truths.
rows.anchor: أحدها : قال مجاهد : تلك النعمة هي القرآن ، فإن القرآن أعظم ما أنعم الله به على محمد عليه السلام

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also identifies the blessing as prophethood, which the Prophet must communicate.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : روي أيضا عن مجاهد : أن تلك النعمة هي النبوة ، أي بلغ ما أنزل إليك من ربك

rows.speaker: الحسين بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Husayn says that when God enables good conduct toward orphans and seekers, one may tell one's brothers so they imitate it, provided there is no ostentation and imitation is expected.
rows.anchor: ومنه ما روي عن الحسين بن علي عليه السلام أنه قال : إذا عملت خيرا فحدث إخوانك ليقتدوا بك

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: When asked to speak about himself after praising the Companions, Ali initially objected that God forbids self-purification, then cited this verse and said he gives when asked, is offered things unasked, and holds abundant knowledge.
rows.anchor: فقالوا له : فحدثنا عن نفسك فقال : مهلا ، فقد نهى الله عن التزكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's right follows the rights of orphans and supplicants because He is self-sufficient while they are needy; their commands require action, while His is fulfilled through speech.
rows.anchor: كأنه يقول أنا غني وهما محتاجان وتقديم حق المحتاج أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse ends the acts of worship with heart and tongue recounting God's favors, keeping Him in remembrance; fa-haddith suggests repeated telling more than fa-khabbir.
rows.anchor: واختار قوله : { فحدث } على قوله فخبر ، ليكون ذلك حديثا عند لا ينساه ، ويعيده مرة بعد أخرى

rows.speaker: طاوس وعمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: They treated al-Duha and al-Sharh as one surah, recited them in one prayer unit, and omitted the basmala between them because the next opening seemed connected.
rows.anchor: يروى عن طاووس وعمر بن عبدالعزيز أنهما كانا يقولان هذه السورة وسورة الضحى سورة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects that inference: al-Duha descended amid grief from persecution, whereas al-Sharh describes an open chest and contentment, different circumstances.
rows.anchor: لأن الأول : كان نزوله حال اغتمام الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من إيذاء الكفار فكانت حال محنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question denying expansion is a reproachful interrogation that affirms and establishes that God expanded the Prophet's chest.
rows.anchor: استفهم عن انتفاء الشرح على وجه الإنكار ، فأفاد إثبات الشرح وإيجابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation reports Gabriel opening Muhammad's chest, removing and washing his heart free of sins, then filling it with knowledge and faith.
rows.anchor: ما روى أن جبريل عليه السلام أتاه وشق صدره وأخرج قلبه وغسله وأنقاه من المعاصي

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The judge objects that this childhood event would be a miracle before prophethood, that washing removes physical things rather than sins, and that only God creates knowledge in a heart.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الواقعة إنما وقعت في حال صغره عليه السلام وذلك من المعجزات ، فلا يجوز أن تتقدم نبوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that a miracle may precede the commission as irhas, and such precursors are common in the Prophet's case.
rows.anchor: عن الأول : أن تقويم المعجز على زمان البعثة جائز عندنا ، وذلك هو المسمى بالإرهاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The removed black blood can signify a heart inclined to sin and reluctant to obey; its removal signals the person's steadfast obedience and provides angels an indication of sinlessness.
rows.anchor: أن يكون حصول ذلك الدم الأسود الذي غسلوه من قلب الرسول عليه السلام علامة للقلب الذي يميل إلى المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes chest expansion as knowledge and obedience, preparing him for the universal mission and its hardships by removing distractions of family, wealth, and fear.
rows.anchor: لما بعث إلى الجن والإنس فكان يضيق صدره عن منازعة الجن والإنس والبراءة من كل عابد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This spiritual expansion means knowing the world's insignificance and the afterlife's perfection; sincere faith produces detachment, longing for the eternal home, and readiness for death.
rows.anchor: فشرح الصدر عبارة عن علمه بحقارة الدنيا وكما الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When asked about the sign of an expanded chest, the Prophet reportedly answered: detachment from delusion, turning toward the eternal home, and preparing for death before it comes.
rows.anchor: قال : ( التجافي عن الغرور ، والإنابة إلى دار الخلود ، والإعداد للموت قبل نزوله )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further meaning is an extraordinary capacity to carry all duties calmly in hardship and ease; expansion relieves worry, which Arabs describe as constricting the chest.
rows.anchor: أنه انفتح صدره حتى أنه كان يتسع لجميع المهمات لا يقلق ولا يضجر ولا يتغير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chest is named because Satan's whispering occurs there; expansion removes whispering and replaces it with good impulses.
rows.anchor: لأن محل الوسوسة هو الصدر على ما قال : { يوسوس فى صدور الناس }

rows.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
rows.claim: The heart is the seat of reason and knowledge, guarded by the chest; if Satan enters the chest he brings worry, grief, and greed, constricting the heart and spoiling worship, while early resistance restores ease.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن علي الترمذي : القلب محل العقل والمعرفة ، وهو الذي يقصده الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'for you' may indicate reciprocity: the Prophet performs all worship for God, and God performs His acts for the Prophet; alternatively, the mission's benefit returns to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : أن فيها تنبيها على أن منافع الرسالة عائدة إليه عليه السلام ، كأنه تعالى قال : إنما شرحنا صدرك لأجلك لا لأجلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using 'We' either magnifies the gift beyond comprehension or includes God's angels, whose presence strengthened the Prophet and made his opponents afraid.
rows.anchor: إن حملناه على نون التعظيم ، فالمعنى أن عظمة المنعم تدل على عظمة النعمة

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad says the conjunction follows the meaning of 'Did We not expand?'—'We expanded'—rather than its surface form; otherwise it should read 'and We place.'
rows.anchor: قال المبرد : هذا محمول على معنى ألم نشرح لا على لفظه ، لأنك لا تقول ألم وضعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wizr is the weight of sin, as in the verse about carrying burdens, and is compared to God's forgiveness of the Prophet's earlier and later sin.
rows.anchor: معنى الوزر ثقل الذنب ، وقد مر تفسيره عند قوله : { وهم يحملون أوزارهم }

rows.speaker: علماء اللغة
rows.claim: Linguists explain anqaḍ as the faint sound a heavily loaded back makes; the phrase metaphorically evokes burdens weighing on the Prophet.
rows.anchor: الأصل فيه أن الظهر إذا أثقل الحمل سمع له نقيض أي صوت خفي

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: Those who allow minor sins for prophets take the burden as one of these, despite its severity, because the Prophet deeply regretted it and its effect on reward was serious though forgiven.
rows.anchor: الذين يجوزون الصغائر على الأنبياء عليهم السلام حملوا هذه الآية عليها

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi objects that if forgiveness of a minor sin is obligatory, it cannot be a favor for which God takes credit.
rows.anchor: وهو أن العفو عن الصغيرة واجب على الله تعالى عند القاضي ، والله تعالى ذكر هذه الآية في معرض الامتنان

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the burden was sins committed before prophethood, which God forgave.
rows.anchor: أحدها : قال قتادة : كانت للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذنوب سلفت منه في الجاهلية قبل النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead be the heavy duties of prophecy, which God made easy to carry and fulfill.
rows.anchor: أن المراد منه تخفيف أعباء النبوة التي تثقل الظهر من القيام بأمرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposal is distress at the changes people made to Abraham's religion, which Muhammad could not stop until God strengthened him and commanded him to follow Abraham.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : الوزر ما كان يكرهه من تغييرهم لسنة الخليل . وكان لا يقدر على منعهم إلى أن قواه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sins of the Prophet's community may have weighed on him; God reassured him against their immediate punishment and promised his intercession in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : أنها ذنوب أمته صارت كالوزر عليه ، ماذا يصنع في حقهم إلى أن قال : { وما كان الله ليعذبهم وأنت فيهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The 'burden' may be a figurative removal of a sin that would have crushed him: before prophethood God once made him sleep through a wedding with music.
rows.anchor: وخامسها : معناه عصمناك عن الوزر الذي ينقض ظهرك ، لو كان ذلك الذنب حاصلا ، فسمى العصمة وضعا مجازا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may have been the terror of first meeting Gabriel: Muhammad shook and nearly threw himself from a mountain, then grew familiar with him and longed to see him.
rows.anchor: وسادسها : الوزر ما أصابه من الهيبة والفزع في أول ملاقاة جبريل عليه السلام ، حين أخذته الرعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may be the abuse and insults that first shook him and nearly crushed his back; later he endured even bloodied attacks while praying for his people.
rows.anchor: ما كان يلحقه من الأذى والشتم حتى كاد ينقض ظهره وتأخذه الرعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the surah followed the deaths of Abu Talib and Khadija, their loss was a great burden; God lifted it by taking him heavenward, where angels greeted him and his renown rose.
rows.anchor: وثامنها : لئن كان نزول السورة بعد موت أبي طالب وخديجة ، فلقد كان فراقهما عليه وزرا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The burden may be pre-prophetic perplexity about how to serve God amid unceasing blessings; revelation clarified how he should worship, easing the shame of inadequate service.
rows.anchor: وتاسعها : أن المراد من الوزر والثقل الحيرة التي كانت له قبل البعثة ، وذلك أنه بكمال عقله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command follows past and promised blessings by urging gratitude and strenuous worship; nasab means to toil, and the general rule is to replace one act of worship with another without leaving time empty.
rows.anchor: وجه تعلق هذا بما قبله أنه تعالى لما عدد عليه نعمه السالفة ، ووعدهم بالنعم الآتية ، لا جرم بعثه على الشكر والاجتهاد في العبادة

rows.speaker: قتادة والضحاك ومقاتل
rows.claim: After the obligatory prayer, stand in supplication and ask God, who will give you what you request.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة والضحاك ومقاتل : إذا فرغت من الصلاة المكتوبة { فانصب * إلى ربك } في الدعاء وارغب إليه

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi interprets it as praying for worldly and next-worldly needs after the tashahhud.
rows.anchor: وقال الشعبي : إذا فرغت من التشهد فادع لدنياك وآخرتك

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says that when worldly affairs are finished, one should rise and pray.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد : إذا فرغت من أمر دنياك فانصب وصل

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah says that after fulfilling the required prayers, one should exert oneself in night worship.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله : إذا فرغت من الفرائض فانصب في قيام الليل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says that after a campaign, one should devote oneself to worship.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن : إذا فرغت من الغزو فاجتهد في العبادة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة
rows.claim: Ali ibn Abi Talha says that when healthy and free, one should spend that leisure in worship.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة : إذا كنت صحيحا فانصب ، يعني اجعل فراغك نصبا في العبادة

rows.speaker: شريح
rows.claim: Passing two men wrestling, Shurayh rebuked them as idle people, since the verse commands effort when free.
rows.anchor: يدل عليه ما روى أن شريحا مر برجلين يتصارعان ، فقال : الفارغ ما أمر بهذا إنما قال الله : { فإذا فرغت فانصب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is to direct desire exclusively to God, seek only His favor, and rely on Him.
rows.anchor: اجعل رغبتك إليه خصوصا ولا تسأل إلا فضله متوكلا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, seek from God everything desired in religion and worldly life, including victory over enemies; a variant reading means urging people to seek what God has.
rows.anchor: ارغب في سائر ما تلتمسه دينا ودنيا ونصرة على الأعداء إلى ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address may turn to humanity generally: anyone declaring a real event unreal lies, so what compels you to deny the resurrection?
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه خطاب للإنسان على طريقة الالتفات ، والمراد من قوله : { فما يكذبك } أن كل من أخبر عن الواقع بأنه لا يقع فهو كاذب

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra' prefers that the question address Muhammad: after these proofs, who can deny the Judgment to you, Messenger?
rows.anchor: والثاني : وهو اختيار الفراء أنه خطاب مع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ، والمعنى فمن يكذبك يا أيها الرسول بعد ظهور هذه الدلائل بالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human formation from a drop into maturity and subsequent decline in old age plainly proves power to resurrect; denying resurrection after seeing it is astonishing.
rows.anchor: أن خلق الإنسان من النطفة وتقويمع بشرا سويا وتدريجه في مراتب الزيادة إلى أن يكمل ويستوي ، تم تنكيسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation confirms that the wise creator's formation and aging of humanity proves both the possibility of resurrection by power and its occurrence by wisdom; otherwise creation would be pointless.
rows.anchor: أن هذا تحقيق لما ذكر من خلق الإنسان ثم رده إلى أرذل العمر ، يقول الله تعالى : أليس الذي فعل ذلك بأحكم الحاكمين صنعا وتدبيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation reassures the Prophet that God will judge fairly between him and his opponents on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: أن هذا تنبيه من الله تعالى لنبيه عليه السلام بأنه يحكم بينه وبين خصومه يوم القيامة بالعدل

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi argues that calling God the wisest rules out His creating human acts: otherwise every foolish act and encouragement to folly would come from Him.
rows.anchor: لو كان الفاعل لأفعال العباد هو الله تعالى لكان كل سفه وكل أمر بسفه وكل ترغيب في سفه فهو من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi replies by invoking knowledge and motive and distinguishes bearing foolishness from creating it: a foolish person bears the trait, just as a mover bears movement without creating it.
rows.anchor: والجواب : المعارضة بالعلم والداعي ، ثم نقول : السفيه من قامت السفاهة به لا من خلق السفاهة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda treats the bāʾ as extra, so the phrase means 'read the name of your Lord'; al-Akhtal's line uses bāʾ before 'the surahs' as evidence.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : الباء زائدة ، والمعنى : اقرأ اسم ربك ، كما قال الأخطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the extra-bāʾ reading: the Prophet's 'I am not a reader' would not answer an instruction to invoke God, the command would be redundant, and it needlessly discards the bāʾ.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنه لو كان معناه اذكر اسم ربك ما حسن منه أن يقول : ما أنا بقارىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qirāʾa here means reciting the Qur'an, as supported by commands elsewhere to follow and recite it to people gradually.
rows.anchor: القول الثاني : أن المراد من قوله : { اقرأ } أي اقرأ القرآن ، إذ القراءة لا تستعمل إلا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading with God's name may mean beginning with the basmala, parsed adverbially; Razi says this supports requiring it at the start of every surah against those who omit it.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن يكون محل باسم ربك النصب على الحال فيكون التقدير : اقرأ القرآن مفتتحا باسم ربك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the basmala is an instrument of seeking God's help, as writing is done with a pen, especially when the Prophet said he could not read.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المعنى اقرأ القرآن مستعينا باسم ربك كأنه يجعل الاسم آلة فيما يحاوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading in God's name can mean dedicating the act to Him; invoking God's ownership also deters Satan from sharing a meal, and a neutral act can become worship when it supports obedience.
rows.anchor: أي اجعل هذا الفعل لله وافعله لأجله كما تقول : بنيت هذه الدار باسم الأمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Allah is a loftier name than rabb, the command uses Lord because worship follows divine acts, not the bare attributes of essence; the title also reassures a frightened Prophet that his nurturer will complete His care.
rows.anchor: وجوابه : أنه أمر بالعبادة ، وبصفات الذات ، وهو لا يستوجب شيئا ، وإنما يستوجب العبادة بصفات الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God 'your Lord' may signal His care for the servant; alternatively, God's benefit flows to the servant first, and after obedience He names him 'My servant.'
rows.anchor: تارة يضيف ذاته إليه بالربوبية كما ههنا ، وتارة يضيفه إلى نفسه بالعبودية ، أسرى بعبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'who created' answers how He is Muhammad's Lord: Muhammad was once nonexistent and then created, so a creator gave him existence and nurtured him.
rows.anchor: لأنك كنت بذاتك وصفاتك معدوما . ثم صرت موجودا فلا بد لك في ذاتك وصفاتك من خالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Three grammatical readings are offered: 'created' may have no object, asserting God alone creates; an unqualified object may mean everything, with humans singled out for honor or because revelation addresses them; or the next phrase explains the initially general creation to magnify humanity.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أن يكون قوله : { الذى خلق } لا يقدر له مفعول ، ويكون المعنى أنه الذي حصل منه الخلق

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: The theologians argue that creation uniquely distinguishes God's essence and cannot be shared, making the power to originate the mark of divinity; prophets identify God as creator, not idols fashioned by people.
rows.anchor: احتج الأصحاب بهذه الآية على أنه لا خالق غير الله تعالى ، قالوا : لأنه سبحانه جعل الخالقية صفة مميزة لذات الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse gradually leads idolaters to acknowledge God: they admit He created them, unlike idols they carved, then concede that creator and noncreator cannot be equal.
rows.anchor: لكن اذكر لهم أنهم هم الذين خلقوا من العلقة فلا يمكنهم إنكاره ، ثم قل : ولا بد للفعل من فاعل

rows.speaker: المتكلمون
rows.claim: Theologians agree the first obligation is knowing God, considering how to know Him, or resolving to undertake that inquiry, according to their well-known disagreement.
rows.anchor: اتفق المتكلمون على أن أول الواجبات معرفة الله تعالى ، أو النظر في معرفة الله أو القصد إلى ذلك النظر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument also rules out natural causation: a created influence requires another cause, while an eternal cause must be either necessitated or voluntary; ordered, beneficial change indicates a knowing agent with choice.
rows.anchor: ودلت الآية على أن القول بالطبع باطل ، لأن المؤثر فيه إن كان حادثا افتقر إلى مؤثر آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural 'clinging clots' follows the generic, collective sense of 'human,' as in the statement that humanity is in loss.
rows.anchor: إنما قال : { من علق } على الجمع لأن الإنسان في معنى الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command to read may first address personal learning and then teaching others, learning from Gabriel and then instructing, or reading in prayer and outside prayer.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : اقرأ أولا لنفسك ، والثاني للتبليغ أو الأول للتعلم من جبريل والثاني للتعليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Generosity gives what benefits another without compensation; praise, reward, and escaping blame all count as compensation, so God cannot act to gain an end without becoming dependent and deficient.
rows.anchor: المسألة الثانية : الكرم إفادة ما ينبغي لا لعوض ، فمن يهب السكين ممن يقتل به نفسه فهو ليس بكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is most generous because He increases benefaction after wrongdoing, as the cited poem says greater failure brings greater favor.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنه كم من كريم يحلم وقت الجناية ، لكنه لا يبقى إحسانه على الوجه الذي كان قبل الجناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's generosity is pure, unlike human generosity that gains praise, reward, or protection from harm.
rows.anchor: أما أنا فالأكرم إذ لا أفعله إلا لمحض الكرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may be the most generous because He originates every kindness, whose generosity is free of deficiency.
rows.anchor: أنه الأكرم لأن له الابتداء في كل كرم وإحسان وكرمه غير مشوب بالتقصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title may encourage reading because God rewards each letter tenfold, urge sincerity beyond expectation, or embolden the Prophet to preach without fear because God will support him.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون هذا حثا على القراءة أي هذا الأكرم لأنه يجازيك بكل حرف عشرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity rises from the lowly clot to knowledge of realities, proving a wise governor guides this change; knowledge is the noblest human trait and God's greatest gift.
rows.anchor: أول حوال الإنسان كونه علقة وهي أخس الأشياء وآخر أمره هو صيرورته عالما بحقائق الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation of the clot-grown human provides rational proof of power, wisdom, knowledge, and mercy; teaching by the pen points to revealed rulings known through transmission, so knowledge of lordship precedes and grounds prophethood.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الدلالة العقلية الدالة على كمال القدرة والحكمة والعلم والرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen may signify writing, which conveys hidden matters, or directly mean teaching people to write; both readings emphasize writing's merit.
rows.anchor: أن المراد من القلم الكتابة التي تعرف بها الأمور الغائبة ، وجعل القلم كناية عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report has Solomon ask a demon about speech: speech is a passing wind, while writing binds it; the ensuing praise presents the pen as a hunter of knowledge, preserving learning across time.
rows.anchor: يروى أن سليمان عليه السلام سأل عفريتا عن الكلام ، فقال : ريح لا يبقى ، قال : فما قيده / قال : الكتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pen's silent mark is heard across east and west, makes religion luminous with black ink, and preserves knowledge; unlike the pen, the tongue cannot be replaced by writing.
rows.anchor: فكذا القلم لا ينطق ثم يسمع الشرق والفرب ، فسبحانه من قادر بسوادها جعل الدين منورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may refer to God's teaching by pen and also to other instruction, with a conjunction omitted; or both clauses may mean that the pen taught humanity what it did not know, the second explaining the first.
rows.anchor: فيحتمل أن يكون المراد علمه بالقلم وعلمه أيضا غير ذلك ولم يذكر واو النسق
